territorial_scope.description: The Regulations are made under the Kenyan Data Protection Act and apply to data controllers and processors that must register under it; the text states no express territorial limit.

evidence.quote: every data controller and data processor shall be required to register in accordance with the provisions of the Act and these Regulations

summary.short: Kenyan regulations under the Data Protection Act that require every data controller and data processor to register with the Data Commissioner, set application, renewal and change-notification procedures and fees, and exempt small entities that do not process Third Schedule purposes.
summary.long: The Regulations, made under section 18 of the Data Protection Act (Cap. 411C), set the procedure for registering data controllers and data processors with the Data Commissioner. Every controller and processor must register (reg. 4), and a controller is a person who determines the purpose and means of processing. Applications use Form DPR1, attach establishment documents and descriptions of purposes and data categories, and pay fees in the Second Schedule (reg. 5). The Commissioner verifies the application, issues a certificate within fourteen days, and the certificate is valid for twenty-four months (regs. 7-9). Refusals must be notified with reasons within twenty-one days, and renewal follows the same process (regs. 10-12). Entities with fewer than ten employees and turnover or revenue below KES 5 million are exempt from mandatory registration, except where they process purposes listed in the Third Schedule, and they must still comply with Parts IV and VI of the Act (reg. 13). The Office publishes a list of registered entities every thirty days, and changes must be notified within fourteen days (regs. 14-15). The Commissioner may cancel or vary certificates on listed grounds (reg. 16). Processing without registration, providing false information, and continuing processing after non-renewal are offences (reg. 18). The header gives commencement as 14 January 2022, while reg. 1(2) sets six months from publication.

relations.note: Regulations made under the Act, procedure under section 18 of the Act; other Act sections are cited in regs 11, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18 (single row for the Act).

evidence.quote: These Regulations provide for the procedure for registration of data controllers and data processors as provided under section 18 of the Act.

relations.note: These Regulations do not apply to civil registration entities specified under that instrument.

evidence.quote: These Regulations shall not apply to civil registration entities specified under the Data Protection (Civil Registration) Regulations (sub. leg).

relations.note: The Data Commissioner is to be guided by this Act before cancelling or varying a registration.

evidence.quote: be guided by the provisions of the Fair Administrative Actions Act, 2015 (Cap. 7J).

notes: Commencement conflict: reg. 1(2) says the regulations take effect six months from publication, but the header states 'Commenced on 14 January 2022' (publication date also 14 January 2022). Reg. 13(2) exempts small controllers and processors from mandatory registration, while reg. 13(5) requires the same entities to register under Part III of the Act. Reg. 4(1) is made subject to 'regulation 13(1)', which holds definitions, while the exemption sits in 13(2). Employee bands differ: Form DPR 1 uses 1-9, 10-49, 50-99, more than 99; the Second Schedule uses 1-50, 51-99, more than 99; reg. 13(2)(b) uses fewer than ten. Header metadata says revised 31 December 2022 by 24th Annual Supplement (Legal Notice 221 of 2023), a date/number mismatch and a consolidation note rather than a relation in this text. Offence penalties (regs 15(4), 18) are by reference to section 73 of the Act; no amounts appear here. Fees are in KES in the Second Schedule.
